trust_decision.summary: Format readers trust the file to supply at most three translation-vector (Tv / lattice) rows and write each one into a fixed vector3 translationVectors[3] stack array, with no bound on the counter.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names MOPAC translationVectors[] in the UNIT CELL TRANSLATION block; that block is at src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:157-175 and writes at line 170.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/formats/gaussformat.cpp:625 and src/formats/msiformat.cpp:157 (other formats' readers with their own translationVectors[3]); also MOPAC input reader src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:729

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about MOPAC output's UNIT CELL TRANSLATION block; the Gaussian and MSI readers are different file formats with separate CVEs (46291, 46295), so a solver could call them out of scope. This argument is weak because one grep for translationVectors[numTranslationVectors++] finds all of them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: 1-D/2-D periodic inputs with fewer than 3 Tv vectors are legitimate. MOPAC input documents up to 3 Tv vectors for 1D/2D/3D. The mopcrt and Gaussian readers attach a unit cell when 1-3 vectors are present. A fix that rejects the file or requires exactly 3 vectors breaks polymer/slab inputs, and so does dropping the unit cell on >3 rows.

O6_input_shapes: more than 3 rows in the MOPAC output UNIT CELL TRANSLATION block (5-column rows)
more than 3 Tv Z-component rows in MOPAC output FINAL POINT AND DERIVATIVES (8-column rows)
more than 3 Tv element lines in MOPAC Cartesian input (6- or 7-token lines, with or without a () label)
more than 3 atomicNum <= 0 rows in a Gaussian orientation block (5- or 6+-column g94/later layouts)
more than 3 6-token vector lines after PeriodicType in MSI

O7_producer.where: Each format reader parses and writes the array directly; OBUnitCell::SetData only consumes the result (src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:483)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The PRIMVEC/CONVVEC loop reads rows until a short line instead of using 'numTranslationVectors < 3 &&'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same idiom as the MOPAC/MSI loops (getline until the token count changes). A maintainer handling animated XSF with repeated blocks could easily write it that way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The rprim loop iterates while vs.size() >= 3 instead of a fixed i < 4
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Other blocks in the same function use while(vs.size()==3) loops (src/formats/abinitformat.cpp:142), so a while-based rprim loop would look natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The (ANGSTROMS) geometry block also collects its skipped Tv rows into translationVectors
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The block already recognises Tv rows at line 142 and discards them; newer MOPAC prints Tv there, so collecting them is a plausible feature.

O9_family: memory-safety: stack out-of-bounds write (fixed-size array indexed by an unbounded, file-controlled counter)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C++ compiler (gcc/clang); an ASan build is needed to detect a 2-element stack overflow reliably
O10_build.project_tests: test/fuzzregresstest.cpp (ctest fuzzregress_1..4 at pinned, test/CMakeLists.txt:35), which reads corpus files from test/files/fuzz_regress/ and relies on a sanitizer; the fix adds parts 5-9
